name: LightCraft

limitations: - OpenGL: AROS One 1.3 has only Mesa's software renderer, so AUTO uses CPU
there. GPU works with it but draws a frame in seconds; use it only to try.

aros-x86_64-abiv1-pc.system: AROS x86_64, mainline ABIv1 (nightly 2026-11-06 or later)
aros-x86_64-abiv1-pc.sdk: x86_64 mainline ABIv1 SDK of nightly 2026-11-10
limitations: - AUTO uses CPU on this system: a program that has opened OpenGL leaves its
log file in use after it ends, and the Shell it ran in stops redirecting
the output of later programs (seen on nightly 2026-11-10). GPU opens
OpenGL all the same; with VirGL in an emulator it drew correctly. Hardware
OpenGL drivers have not been tested.

aros-aarch64-abiv1-raspi.system: AROS on Raspberry Pi, AArch64 ABIv1 (nightly 2026-11-06 or later)
aros-aarch64-abiv1-raspi.sdk: Raspberry Pi AArch64 ABIv1 SDK of nightly 2026-11-10
limitations: - OpenGL has not been tested on Pi hardware, so AUTO uses CPU. GPU opens
OpenGL; save your work before you try it.
- Tested in an emulator only, not on a physical Raspberry Pi.
- Developing and exporting run on the processor; the GPU setting has no
effect. Large raw files and the generated demo photos take time on slow
machines and in emulators.
- Not built in: AI Denoise, AI masks and HEIC/HEIF import. AVIF files can
be exported but not imported.
- Use a library in one LightCraft (window or lightcraft-cli) at a time: the
library cannot be locked against a second program on AROS.
- Links, other programs (Edit In, Open With) and folder windows are not
opened from LightCraft. The low-disk warning is not shown.
- Chinese, Japanese and Korean fonts are not built in; such text shows as
boxes.
- Changes of the whole window (scrolling, zooming, opening a dialog) redraw
all of it; on slow machines and in emulators these follow with a delay.
- Not tested on AROS in this release: Workbench start, the file requesters,
the clipboard, keyboard layouts other than the US one, printing, the
slideshow, Lightroom import and the MCP server beyond its handshake.
- No automatic updates: install new versions with the AROS package manager
or by unpacking the new archive.
